page: Microsoft Azure E48ads_v7 is a memory-optimized virtual machine built on AMD EPYC 9V45 processors operating at up to 4.5 GHz. Configured on Microsoft Hyper-V, the instance supplies 48 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 24 physical cores with multithreading enabled. The x86_64 architecture incorporates AVX-512 extensions (including VNNI and BF16) and cryptographic acceleration such as VAES and SHA-NI. The host platform features 48 KB of L1 data cache, 1 MB of L2 cache, and 32 MB of L3 cache per core cluster.

System memory is provisioned at 384.0 GB, maintaining an 8:1 memory-to-vCPU ratio of 8.0 GB per vCPU. The node also includes 2,832 GB of direct-attached NVMe SSD local storage for temporary scratch space, cache arrays, or swap partitions. There are no discrete hardware GPUs attached to the instance, and complimentary public IPv4 addresses are not included.

Benchmark outcomes demonstrate top-tier execution across single-threaded and memory-bound tasks. The instance records a Geekbench single-core score of 2,808.0 and a multi-core score of 24,409.0, both placing in the top 10%. Memory subsystem benchmarks reflect strong results, with PassMark memory testing reaching 2,973.22 points and cached read bandwidth hitting 5,034.16 GB/sec. Uncached large-block read throughput registers at 153.47 GB/sec, while write operations reach 103.08 GB/sec.

Data manipulation throughput is consistent, logging 78.13 million operations per second in Redis SET tests and 28,838.61 in PassMark database operations. In lightweight CPU-based language model workloads, prompt processing reaches 4,453.7 tokens per second on 135M parameter models, but throughput moderates to 15.15 tokens per second on 70B parameter models due to the absence of dedicated matrix accelerators. Given its resource density and fast local NVMe capacity, the E48ads_v7 offers a balanced profile for enterprise in-memory caches, relational database systems, and heavy memory-bound analytics pipelines.
description: Microsoft Azure E48ads_v7 is a memory-optimized virtual machine featuring 48 vCPUs and 24 physical cores powered by an AMD EPYC 9V45 processor clocked up to 4.5 GHz. Operating on the Microsoft Hyper-V platform, it includes 384.0 GB of system memory, matching an 8.0 GB per vCPU profile, alongside 2,832 GB of integrated local NVMe SSD storage. The x86_64 CPU supports AVX-512, BF16, and hardware cryptographic instruction sets, but lacks a dedicated GPU. Performance testing highlights top-tier results in Geekbench single-core and multi-core evaluations, top-tier PassMark memory scores, and strong data-tier metrics reaching 78.13 million operations per second on Redis SET benchmarks. The system delivers strong cost efficiency for high-capacity memory pools paired with high-speed local scratch storage. Its hardware configuration fits in-memory key-value databases, analytics engines, relational database instances, and enterprise data processing tasks.
